_comment: temper-design-bundle's expected-failure manifest, the sibling of
Same contract -- see wasm_expected_failures.json's _comment for why divergences are
LISTED and executed rather than deleted or cfg'd out.
This one is EMPTY, and that is a result rather than an omission: measured 2026-08-10
against 24 registered tests, all 24 execute and all 24 pass on
wasm32-unknown-unknown. What survives --no-default-features here is s-expression and
netlist parsing, board identity, PCL constraint typing and constraint merging: no
clock, no dynamic loader, no entropy, no libm edge cases, so none of the four
established divergence classes has anything to attach to.
The file still exists because run_wasm_tests.mjs defaults to the temper-drc-rs
manifest, and pointing a design-bundle-only module at THAT one would report every
drc entry as an orphan exclusion and exit non-zero. `make wasm-design-bundle-test`
passes this file. It is also where a future divergence gets recorded, so the shape
is already right when one appears.
An empty manifest is NOT a weaker gate. run_wasm_tests.mjs still fails the run on any
unexpected failure, so with nothing excluded here every one of the 24 tests is
load-bearing: a regression on wasm32 turns the step red immediately.
